headlines.title: Monterey County investigators believe teen mother of deceased ‘Baby Angelita' may have run over the infant
headlines.description: A newborn infant found deceased in Monterey County over two months ago may have been run over by a vehicle being driven by the baby’s 14-year-old mother, county and federal law enforcement said Thursday at a press conference. An infant dubbed “Baby Angelita” was found deceased on Aug. 1 and detectives determined that the child’s 14-year-old mother had been impregnated by her own father, Sergio Galvez Perez. An Amber Alert went out for both of them on Sept. 6 and the Monterey County Sheriff’s Office said Sunday that the pair were located by authorities in Mexico. On Thursday, Sheriff Tina Nieto, the FBI and other law enforcement shed more light on the case that has brought criticism to the Sheriff’s Office and widespread concern about the 14-year-old’s well-being. Thursday was the first time officials revealed that they believe the girl delivered the baby next to a strawberry field in an unincorporated part of the county where she was a laborer and then may have run it over with her vehicle. Evidence at the scene allegedly pointed to the infant being run over by a car, including evidence showing that it was the right front wheel of the sedan, according to Detective Richard Geng with the Sheriff’s Office. “Several feet from Baby Angelita was what appeared to be a large blood stain, which led detectives to believe that Baby Angelita was moved from where she was born to a location under a vehicle that ended up running her over,” Geng said. The vehicle was caught on license plate readers arriving at and leaving the worksite that day and was connected to the 14-year-old’s parents. Investigators believe the girl hid her pregnancy from her mother and that her father was not in the area on the day of the infant’s death. Later that day, law enforcement went to the Salinas home of Galvez Perez and the girl’s mother, Ofelia Garcia Ortega. The girl was found hiding under a pile of clothing and all three were taken to the station for questioning. Initially, the girl told investigators that she had been impregnated by another juvenile, but it was later determined that it had been her father. She was taken to the hospital for post-childbirth care, but her father removed her on Aug. 4 and the two went to Mexico, the Sheriff’s Office said. The case garnered a lot of attention after Nieto initially announced that there was probable cause to arrest the teen for murder. The Sheriff’s Office also initially said the case did not meet the right criteria for an Amber Alert to be issued. Pushback from county Supervisor Wendy Root Askew and the community led the District Attorney’s Office to release a statement that it hadn’t yet charged the girl with anything. Prosecutors have, however, filed charges against Galvez Perez “for the heinous crime of sexually assaulting his own child.” Law enforcement at the press conference Thursday said they have no evidence tying Galvez Perez to the death of the infant and said he was in the Bay Area at the time. Both Galvez Perez and the girl remain in Mexico, though Monterey County authorities are working on extraditing him. They did not comment on whether the 14-year-old girl would be extradited or charged. The girl’s mother was arrested this week in Salinas on suspicion of displaying or possessing a forged identification card, permitting a child to suffer or be endangered, and contributing to the delinquency of a minor.
headlines.source: Katy St. Clair | Bay City News

headlines.title: Memory card with wedding day photos stolen from photographer's vehicle in Oakland
headlines.description: A wedding photographer’s vehicle got broken into in Oakland. He says thieves stole his cameras and equipment, including memory cards that held a couple’s wedding day pictures. Jenna Wesenhagen Banks and Nick Banks got married this past weekend. It was a day spent with their kids and loved ones as they celebrated their love, memories they were hoping to look back on forever. “Our families coming together, it was just something special, and even the photographer, he’s a friend of the family, he’s known my wife’s family for years,” Banks said. David Martin Jr. is a photographer from Antioch but now based out of Southern California. He traveled to the East Bay to photograph his friend Jenna’s wedding on Sunday. On Wednesday, Martin Jr. was on his way to another job when he stopped by Jack London Square in Oakland to get food. That’s when he says his vehicle got broken into. He says thieves stole cameras, lights, a drone, his computer and other gear. “I was over in Swan’s Market, and I came back out to my car, and they smashed my side window and back window,” Martin Jr. said. Martin Jr. said he’ll have to replace tens of thousands of dollars’ worth of equipment, but what he cares about the most are the couple’s wedding photos. Martin Jr. hopes whoever has them now will realize what they took and return the memory cards. “That’s all I really care about. If you’re the people that did this, no questions asked, the photos aren’t worth anything to you, there’s no monetary value for you there, you can keep all the other stuff,” he said. For Nick and Jenna, these photos are irreplaceable. “Pictures of our parents, grandparents, people that aren’t always going to be around as well,” Jenna said. “We just hope and pray that you do the right thing and be a good human being and give us back what we would really would enjoy to have for the rest of our lives and for our kids to see when they get older.”

headlines.title: East Bay residents raise concerns about refineries' safety records at town hall
headlines.description: Following a long history of fires, flaring and pollution at the Martinez refinery and a nearby Renewable Energy Facility, community members aired their concerns on Thursday and asked what’s being done to protect their health. About 100 people from across Contra Costa County packed into John Muir Elementary School’s multi-purpose room to tell their congressman what worries them most about violations and safety records at Martinez Refining Company and neighboring refineries. The town hall came after more than 160 violations were reported at the Martinez refinery since 2020, which resulted in a $10 million penalty levied against the company earlier this year. One of the most notable incidents at the refining operation occurred in February 2025, when a fire produced thick smoke and soot fallout, prompting a four-day long public health advisory. There have also been concerns at the nearby Marathon Martinez Renewable Facility, where a worker was critically injured in a fire in 2023. Workers have also reported other safety concerns in recent months. “The fact that they’re flaring more, and we had that near-fatal accident, tells me that they don’t respect our qualified workforce,” Rep. Mark DeSaulnier said. In a written statement earlier this year, Marathon said it has corrected issues that led to the fire in 2023 and was continuing to address safety and reliability concerns. DeSaulnier has been critical of the safety records at both facilities. “Not with everybody, but some of them want to cut costs, and they want to cut costs with their workforce, which cuts safety programs,” DeSaulnier said. Residents say they want better enforcement, worker protections and more transparency. “I think more could be done to notify the public. People just want to be informed. They want to be safe. They want their children safe, and they want their environment safe,” Stephanie T. said. DeSaulnier has been critical of refinery operations, he also said the companies are critical to the local economy. “As I said, we want you to be successful and profitable, but not at the expense of the community or the workforce,” he said. A public dashboard that lets people report and track incidents in real time is now online. NBC Bay Area reached out to Martinez Refining Company and parent company PBF Energy for comment and have not heard back.

headlines.title: 3 San Francisco police officers face brutality complaints over 2025 arrest
headlines.description: The San Francisco Public Defender’s Office is filing police brutality complaints against three officers in response to what the office called a violent arrest last year. The public defender’s office said the arrest of Kevon Gibson resulted in him needing to spend multiple days in the intensive care unit to recover. Gibson’s arrest happened on Aug. 17, 2025, after police were called to an SRO hotel on Sixth Street. On Thursday, the public defender’s office shared police body camera video of portions of a conversation with a complaining resident at the hotel. “The complainant had threatened Mr. Gibson that morning and then called the police claiming that Gibson had flashed a gun at him,” said Valerie Ibarra, a spokesperson for the public defender’s office. “What he described was actually a torch lighter that Mr. Gibson had in his pocket.” According to the public defender’s office, the three officers then tried to find Gibson at his girlfriend’s apartment in the building. They eventually found him and confronted him in a nearby elevator. In hallway security camera video footage, officers could be seen striking Gibson repeatedly as they wrestled with him on the ground. Gibson’s attorneys said he had to spend days in the intensive care unit after the arrest. The public defender’s office said it’s filing a complaint with San Francisco’s Department of Police Accountability and also plans to file a complaint with state authorities to possibly yank the certifications of the officers based on the video footage. “That shows their state of mind, that they were there to taunt, to target, to harass, basically, our client,” said Angela Chan with the public defender’s office. The case has already circulated through the criminal court system. In August, a jury convicted Gibson of three counts of misdemeanor resisting arrest and being a felon in possession of a firearm. In the hallway security camera video footage, an officer could be seen pulling a gun from Gibson as he was on the ground. Following Gibson’s conviction in August, the district attorney’s office praised the officers for their work. The district attorney’s office issued a statement refuting the accusations and standing by the arrest, saying the suspect was tried and convicted. Neither the police department nor the police union provided any comment.

headlines.title: Deaths in Monte Sereno house fire may have been preventable, investigators say
headlines.description: Investigators said the deaths of a beloved couple in a house fire in Monte Sereno on Wednesday morning might have been preventable. Investigators say the fire broke out around 2 a.m. in a second-floor kitchen, but they cannot determine exactly what caused it to start. Firefighters encountered household materials piled up in the garage, which was the main entryway. “That part of the structure was filled more or less from top to bottom with materials that made passing through very difficult,” Assistant Chief of Operations Bill Murphy said. “To give kind of a visual, in order to get back to where the individuals were in their bedroom, we would have to walk on top of items that were on the floor,” Assistant Chief Fire Prevention Jeremy Davis said. Additionally, firefighters did not find any working smoke detectors. “Based on the location of the occupants when they were recovered, smoke detectors were a factor. I believe, and it is our belief, that if there were smoke detectors, they would’ve allowed for early notification for the decedents, which may have given them an opportunity to get out,” Davis said. Susan, a neighbor and family friend, says all the material in the front of the house, basically used for storage, always made her concerned for the couple’s safety. “And I heard there was a lot of that same kind of material up there. It’s kind of scary,” Susan said. “But it was really piling up… So, when I heard that, I just… it was hard. It still is hard.” The Coroner’s Office has not released the names of the couple. The couple was involved with a local church, which says it will have an official response once the names are made public. The Santa Clara County Fire Department calls the fire “accidental”.

headlines.title: Family of missing Bay Area woman Chantel Brooks launches new search in Vacaville
headlines.description: The family of a Bay Area woman missing for nearly three months searched a new spot on Thursday they say she may have visited around the time she disappeared. Chantel Brooks’ family says one of her brothers had access to her location on the find my iPhone app. They say her phone last pinged at Lagoon Valley Regional Park in Vacaville, prompting them to launch another search. Brooks, 37, was last seen leaving her job at a San Francisco Hotel on July 17. About an hour later, she was seen leaving a Fairfield CVS store and approaching her black SUV, but nobody has seen her since. Though Fairfield police have said they suspect foul play, Brooks’ family say they still have hope. Her brothers and volunteers searched a Vacaville Park both on foot and by drone on Thursday. They say Brooks’ iPhone last pinged at the park around the time she disappeared. “We have to check every area. There’s no stone we’re gonna leave untouched,” Brooks’ brother Kevin Robinson said. April Martin of Vacaville donated water and snacks to the search effort. She doesn’t know Brooks but says the case has hit too close to home. “If it was my child or my sibling I’d want as much help as I could get in today. I woke up and decided I wanted to be a part of it. I wanted to be some help to someone else,” Martin said. Her brothers say they’re grateful for the help. They say they aren’t about to give up on their sister, who they say was the life and love of their family. “I just want her home safe; that’s it if I had one wish right now. I just want her to be safe, that’s it,” Brooks’ brother Calvin Robinson said. Fairfield police said they have no new updates on the case but are still following leads.

headlines.title: Uniqlo to open new flagship store in San Francisco
headlines.description: Uniqlo is set to open a new flagship store in San Francisco on Friday. The clothing retailer is set to open its new flagship at 4th and Market, a space that’s long been vacant. According to the mayor’s office the new store will employ more than 80 people and, hopefully, draw new energy downtown. “Uniqlo is investing in a really big way in 20,000 square foot space right in down Market Street. They had left the area a few years back, and so they decided they really needed to back in our downtown market and we’re thrilled to have them,” Executive Director of the Office of Economic and Workforce Development Anne Taupier said. The retailer has been in San Francisco before, but closed its store on Powell Street in 2021, being one of many retailers that left as the pandemic deepened. These days, the city says they are seeing a big return of retail in downtown and Union Square, and this opening could help send a signal. “I think it sends a signal, and we watch these retailers and other businesses when they see someone investing in a downtown they want to know are missing an opportunity to be downtown,” Taupier said. The store also say it expects to offer exclusive merchandise that embraces the San Francisco spirit through collaboration. There’s also a street festival planned to mark its opening as well. In a statement, the retailer’s United States CEO said in part, “Uniqlo is investing in downtown because we believe in its future and want to be part of the energy returning to the neighborhood.”

headlines.title: Blue Angels practice ahead of San Francisco Fleet Week air shows
headlines.description: The U.S. Navy Blue Angels took to the skies Thursday for a practice session ahead of three straight days of San Francisco Fleet Week air shows. The Blue Angels are known for extreme aerobatics precision, flying as close as 18 inches apart in formation and reaching speeds of up to 700 mph. Thursday’s practice flights provided a chance for the pilots to get familiar with the area and for the team to make sure every move was dialed in before they perform in front of the Fleet Week crowd. “We are looking at all the visual checkpoints that we will use throughout the entire weekend, seeing how our maneuvers will fit into those so we can do them safely and make them look good,” Blue Angels Flight Leader/Commanding Officer Capt. Adam Bryan said. Fleet Week air shows, headlined by the Blue Angels, are scheduled to take place on Friday, Saturday and Sunday. “We are constantly striving to get better in everything that we do and reaching for that perfect flight demonstration squadron and that perfect flight demonstration,” Bryan said. “Hopefully we get it this weekend.” The Blue Angels did not perform during last year’s Fleet Week due to a federal government shutdown, so this year’s return feels extra special for the team. “It’s something that our team marks on our calendar every single year,” Bryan said. “It’s great to see all the landmarks and feel the energy of the city and the entire area.” San Francisco Sep 21 San Francisco 15 hours ago When are the Blue Angels performing? headlines.title: Adjustable-rate mortgages make a comeback in the Bay Area, but there are risks
headlines.description: Adjustable-rate mortgages are making a comeback in the Bay Area as home prices continue to rise. However, this option also carries considerable risk. Real estate agents say more people want the freedom to adjust in today’s high and climbing mortgage rate market. “There’s definitely a trend and a curiosity of adjustable-rate mortgages,” Silicon Valley real estate broker Lynsie Gridley said. What a buyer pays for an adjustable-rate mortgage starts considerably lower than most fixed-rate mortgages. “The spread, or the difference between a fixed rate and an adjustable rate, is often ¾ to 1% difference in rate,” Redwood Credit Union Mortgage Lending Senior VP Debbie Ingle said. That could mean saving more than $1,000 a month in the Bay Area, or about $100,000 in seven years. But because the rate is adjustable, it moves – and that means it comes with a potential dark side. “There is upside risk, because they don’t know where it’s gonna go, they know how long it’s locked at this rate, and then you know you’ll be eventually adjusting and it can adjust up or down,” Gridley said. “You don’t have that level of, ‘I can relax, I’ve got a 30-year fixed payment.’ You have to stay abreast of what’s happening in the real estate market and with interest rates,” Ingle said.

headlines.title: Man charged following crash that killed 2 in Daly City
headlines.description: A 28-year-old San Francisco man is accused of running a red light and crashing into another vehicle in Daly City last weekend, killing two people, San Mateo County prosecutors said Thursday. Alvaro Caballero Arteaga made his initial appearance in court Wednesday to face charges for a crash reported on Sunday at the intersection of San Jose Avenue and Flournoy Street, according to the San Mateo County District Attorney’s Office. Caballero Arteaga allegedly sped through a red light and broadsided another vehicle, killing the driver Rhiannon Lawler and passenger Agustin Garcia, prosecutors said. A preliminary alcohol screening showed he had a blood alcohol level of 0.15%, and investigators learned his driver’s license had been suspended following an arrest in February in Alameda County for misdemeanor drunk driving, according to the district attorney’s office. Caballero Arteaga did not enter a plea at his arraignment Wednesday and was assigned an attorney via the county’s Private Defender Program. He will return to court on Oct. 15 for further arraignment and remains in custody on “no bail” status, prosecutors said.
